gaps.sentence: We stopped at a cafe to ___ a chat.
gaps.explanation: have a chat is the fixed collocation for a friendly, informal conversation.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune selling software online.
gaps.explanation: make a fortune means to earn a very large amount of money.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the blame for the accident onto the weather.
gaps.explanation: 'Shift the blame onto somebody' = transfer responsibility.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: All candidates must ___ the written exam in June.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'exam' from the candidate's side
gaps.explanation: take an exam (or sit an exam) means to be tested; 'give an exam' is not used in British English.

gaps.sentence: You are ___ a big risk if you invest all your money in one company.
gaps.explanation: take a risk means to do something that might have a bad result.
